items.question: Can ClaimVerse support straight-through processing?
items.answer: Yes, for claim journeys and scenarios that meet configured eligibility and decision rules.

items.question: Does ClaimVerse replace an insurer's existing claims core?
items.answer: It can operate as a modern claims workflow and experience layer or as part of a wider claims transformation, depending on the target architecture.

items.question: Can policyholders track claim progress?
items.answer: Claim status and customer communication can be exposed through appropriate digital experiences and integrations.

automation.title: Automate routine claim work. Use intelligence where interpretation is needed.
automation.body: Use workflow automation for tasks, queues, SLA escalation, status communication and straight-through processing. Use intelligent assistance for document understanding, summaries, model-based triage or anomaly signals where validated. Use analytics to measure cycle time, workload, automation and exceptions.
automation.responsibility: Material claim decisions remain under defined human authority.

hero.title: Everything required to orchestrate the digital claims lifecycle.
hero.lede: ClaimVerse is designed around the work required to move a claim from notification through assessment, decision and settlement. It combines customer intake, handler work, workflow, evidence, controls and operational visibility while allowing straightforward and complex claims to follow different paths.

meta.title: ClaimVerse Use Cases | Digital FNOL, Claims Automation & Complex Case Management
meta.description: See how ClaimVerse supports digital FNOL, simple claims, complex case management, provider workflows, investigation, catastrophe intake and settlement.

hero.title: Different claims need different paths.
hero.lede: ClaimVerse can support low-complexity digital journeys, specialist claim handling and high-volume operational scenarios through configurable workflows rather than forcing every claim through the same process. Only lines of business confirmed by the product and implementation teams are described here.

cases.title: Digital FNOL
cases.situation: Customers need to report a claim quickly but may not understand which information or evidence is required.
cases.usage: A guided digital journey captures the initial event, claimant and policy information, documents or images and creates a claim reference before routing the case.
cases.change: Cleaner intake. Faster acknowledgement. Less manual re-keying. Better customer clarity.

cases.title: Low-complexity retail claims
cases.situation: A high volume of straightforward claims consume handler time even when the required information is complete and the claim meets known criteria.
cases.usage: Configured validation, document checks, triage and straight-through rules can allow eligible cases to progress with minimal handling, while exceptions move to a claims specialist.
cases.change: More operational capacity. Faster routine claims. Specialists spend more time on exceptions.

cases.title: Motor claims
cases.situation: Motor claims can involve customer evidence, vehicle details, repairers, assessors, estimates and multiple status updates.
cases.usage: The claim journey can coordinate FNOL, documents and images, assessment, provider activity, approval and customer communication.
cases.change: Better coordination. Clearer repair and assessment status. More consistent customer updates.

cases.title: Travel claims
cases.situation: Travel claims are often document-heavy and customers may be remote or in another market.
cases.usage: Digital intake, supporting-document collection, claim queues, assessment and communication can be managed in a remote-friendly workflow.
cases.change: Less paper. Better document visibility. Easier customer follow-up.

cases.title: Property and catastrophe-related claims
cases.situation: A weather or catastrophe event can create a sudden increase in claim volume and customer enquiries.
cases.usage: Event tagging, digital intake, priority queues, additional work assignment and operational dashboards can help the claim organization manage the surge where scale has been validated.
cases.change: Better event visibility. Faster prioritization. More coordinated customer communication. Catastrophe-scale claims handling is not published until performance and operational capability have been validated.

cases.title: Health or provider-involved claims
cases.situation: Health or provider-related claims can require medical and provider documents, authorizations, specialist review and external communication.
cases.usage: Configured workflows can collect documents, manage provider interaction, route specialist review and maintain status.
cases.change: More structured provider coordination. Better documentation. Clearer workflow ownership.

cases.title: Complex claims case management
cases.situation: Some claims require investigation, multiple specialists, repeated evidence collection and senior authority.
cases.usage: The claim workbench coordinates tasks, documents, investigation activity, referrals, approvals and communication over a longer lifecycle.
cases.change: One clearer case history. Better accountability. Stronger control over referrals and decisions.

cases.title: Fraud or investigation referral
cases.situation: Claims teams need to identify cases that require deeper review without slowing every claim.
cases.usage: Configured rules and available anomaly signals route selected claims into investigation queues with additional tasks and authority controls.
cases.change: More targeted investigation. Less unnecessary friction on routine claims. Better referral traceability.

cases.title: Provider and repair network workflows
cases.situation: The insurer depends on external service providers but lacks visibility into assignments, documents and completion status.
cases.usage: Provider tasks, documents, estimates and status and internal approvals are connected to the claim where the provider model is supported.
cases.change: Clearer external-party coordination. Better handler visibility. Easier customer updates.

cases.title: Settlement and closure
cases.situation: Approved claims can still be delayed by payment preparation, communication or missing closure information.
cases.usage: Decision, settlement information, payment connectivity, customer communication and closure tasks are coordinated in one final workflow.
cases.change: Fewer end-of-process gaps. Better settlement visibility. Cleaner closure.

meta.description: Use AI-assisted claims intake, document processing, triage, fraud signals, claim summaries, next actions, straight-through processing and claims analytics.

hero.title: Let claim professionals spend more time resolving the claim.
hero.lede: Claims teams lose time reading documents, re-keying information, assigning cases, checking completeness, answering routine status questions and preparing repetitive communication.

body: AI can reduce that administrative load while keeping coverage, liability, fraud, settlement and complex customer decisions under human control.

sections.title: Automation, AI and analytics are not the same thing.

features.description: Configured rules and workflows that perform predictable tasks automatically.
Predictive, language, vision or generative capability used to interpret, predict, summarize or recommend.
Dashboards and metrics used to understand performance, and to measure whether automation and intelligence are creating value.

sections.note: We use the word AI only when the capability genuinely depends on AI, not as a label for ordinary workflow automation.

body: AI-assisted voice or chat can guide a customer through first notification, ask relevant follow-up questions and capture structured information where supported.

roles.description: Less call-centre scripting and manual re-keying during routine notification.

body: Classify documents, extract selected fields, summarize reports, identify missing items, link evidence to the claim and surface inconsistencies.
For image and vision capabilities, publish only assessment use cases validated for the current release.

roles.description: Less first-pass document reading and data entry.

body: Create a concise working summary from claim details, timeline, documents, tasks, provider activity and communication.

roles.description: Less time reconstructing the case when it is reassigned or escalated.

body: Use claim type, severity, completeness, product, customer context, risk and fraud signals, and workload to recommend priority and queue.
AI routes for investigation. It should not automatically accuse or deny.
Suggest missing evidence, provider assignment, follow-up task, customer communication or approval step according to claim state.

sections.title: Let eligible routine claims move automatically.
body: Claims meeting defined criteria can progress through validation, routing, approval or settlement preparation with limited touch. Exceptions stop and move to human review.
Draft acknowledgement, missing-information requests, status updates, provider communication and settlement messages for review.

sections.title: See the inventory, the speed and the exceptions.

features.description: Intake-to-assignment, stage time and cycle time.
Missing documents, rework, reopen and exceptions.
Touchless rate, automated tasks and human interventions.
Settlement and payment progress; leakage and reserving only where validated.

body: Measure minutes saved on intake, documents processed automatically, extraction correction rate, triage override rate, straight-through exception rate, handler touches per claim, communication-draft edit rate, investigation precision, cycle-time movement and customer repeat contact.

Keep coverage interpretation, liability decisions, fraud investigation, material settlement decisions and sensitive customer interactions under defined authority. Provide evidence, confidence and exception handling, audit trail, override and escalation.

cta.title: Automate routine claim work without automating away judgement.
